findings.body: **Stored XSS:** `body` is passed to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with no escaping or sanitization after `escapeHtml` was removed. Any comment string containing HTML runs in the reader's origin. Example payload: `` executes script when the comment renders and can exfiltrate session state or act as the user. Restore escaping, render text via React children, or — if rich formatting is required — parse an allowlisted markdown subset to elements, or sanitize HTML with a strict library (tags/attrs allowlist) before setting `__html`. Do not assign raw `body` to `__html`.

summary: ## Verdict Critical XSS regression — do not merge until comment HTML is sanitized or safely rendered. ## Narrative `Comment` previously escaped `&`, `<`, and `>` before feeding `body` into `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, so user text could not introduce tags or attributes. This change deletes `escapeHtml` and assigns `body` straight to `__html`. There is no markdown parser, allowlist, or sanitizer (e.g. DOMPurify) in the tree. Any caller that passes comment text from users, APIs, or stored content will execute arbitrary HTML/JS in the viewer session — classic stored XSS via payloads such as `` or `

verification.reason: The patch removes escapeHtml and passes unsanitized body into dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so any HTML/script in a comment string executes in the reader origin. That is a real stored-XSS regression; critical severity is appropriate.
